evidence: Intro: mycotoxins cause decreased feeding efficiency, milk productivity, etc.
Farms with lower LUR produce more milk; LUR inversely related to milk yield (R2=0.86).
Larger concentrate input associated with higher eFCR/eECR (Table 6 correlations).
AFB1 is one analyte in the sample preparation protocol; "measured by protocol" is an uninformative/inverted relation.
No H+-translocase 2 in paper; garbled entity (monitored mycotoxins list has none).
Paper reports moniliformin (MON), not "monilordin"; entity misspelled/garbled.
Nutrient surplus risk is cited for by-product replacement of cereals reducing it; concentrate increasing it is only implied.
"By-products do not compete with human nutrition, and do not impact land use, since the land is cultivated for human food."
AFB1 measured in roughage (8.33%) and concentrate feeds, found contaminated.
Farms with higher dairy yield showed lower LUR (R2=0.86).
Mycotoxins are produced by mycotoxigenic fungi (Aspergillus, Fusarium etc.).
AFB1 detected in 17% of maize silage and complete feed from dairy farms.
Fusarium listed among most common toxigenic fungi in agricultural products.
Land area of lowland farms was statistically best rated for soil quality and climate.
Paper: increasing milk yield per cow strongly negatively correlates with FCR; "bovine milk reduces FCR" loses the yield/per-cow framing.
LUR concept follows a product LCA approach; LCA does not "determine" land use requirement, relation misstated.
Feed conversion efficiency expressed as reciprocal of FCR/eFCR (reversed ratio).
ENNA found in 4% of seeds, ENNB 11%; low frequencies in maize samples (name spelled enniatrin).
AFG2 found in one maize seed sample (4%, 285.6 ug/kg); triple holds though description says 7%.
AFM1 detected in 69.2% of raw milk samples, mean 7.31 ug/kg.
Inverted/nonsensical: cakes and extraction meals are feed for dairy cows, not "used as dairy cow".
Abstract: improving forage quality may be a suitable strategy to reduce eFCR.
Table 2: high protein concentrate has 489 g CP per kg DM.
Only grass-based systems can use land unsuitable for crops, a LUR mitigation strategy.
AFB1 found at harvest in a single sample (0.8 ug/kg; grain or forage unspecified), not in seeds; "contains" overstated.
